title: HP Omen MAX 16" OLED Gaming Laptop: Intel Ultra 9 275HX CPU, 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD, RTX 5080 GPU $3999.20 Delivered @ HP eBay
body:
Deal: HP Omen MAX 16" OLED Gaming Laptop: Intel Ultra 9 275HX CPU, 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD, RTX 5080 GPU $3999.20 Delivered @ HP eBay

[natoms] Actually not that bad? Considering hardware's price nowadays
For your information, I bought 13900hx+4080 in 3200$ 3 years before
[Wilson80] Thanks for the reply,
Wondering if Cryo compound ever been an issue with your model?
seen some major failure due to leakage, some says PTM7950 is a must for these omen
[natoms] I've heard about this issue before, particularly with the Legion series of laptops.
My own Legion Pro 7i has never experienced this problem; however, as you mentioned, I replaced the factory-applied liquid metal with PTM7950. I also perform this replacement—along with a thorough dust cleaning—quite frequently, roughly every six months. PTM7950 is truly excellent stuff; it carries no risk of leakage and provides more than adequate cooling performance.
[BrainOverFlow] I got my 5070ti one for $1835 a few days ago:
https://www.lenovo.com/au/outlet/en/p/laptops/legion-laptops…
It's used but only with 6 battery cycles, in like-new condition. Suggest monitoring the lenovo outlet for future deals before you pull the trigger.
[deangalanoz] Prices of Lenovo laptops on the outlet site significantly reduces when it's out of stock and can't be purchase.
Someone probably paid $2300+ for that one
[Aureus] They just said they got it for $1835. There are great specials on outlet, but they don't last long.

Any tips on when to look?
[BrainOverFlow] TBH I have no idea, I just set the lenovo outlet legion page as my browser start up then on Oct 26 I saw this one I shared and this one as well around 12 PM: https://www.lenovo.com/au/outlet/en/p/laptops/legion-laptops…
Hope this helps!
[MrZ] 16" is small for $4k. I would want a 17-18" screen for that price.
[MrZ] Still seems like solid value. My first laptop (P133 MMX) in 1997 was this price.
[Pacify] 18 inch laptops are bloody gigantic.
Odds are at home you just going to have it plugged into a monitor, and away who wants to lug around a billion kg laptop
[MrZ] I used to have a 17.3" laptop and it was reasonable size.
[Nom] or is there a potential catch I'm missing?
Do you actually need a laptop ?
A desktop machine is better at gaming in every possible metric you can think of, except that it's not portable. Don't buy a gaming laptop unless you actually need it to be portable 👍
[Nefe] I prefer to have both in one compact machine. It does not perform like a desktop, but do you really need all those FPS? I play RPGs, so no need at all to play in 120Hz, or even in 60FPS, tbh. My MSI laptop has 1.99kg with a RTX 4080, so still quite portable. I've been playing whatever I like
[sickaunt] Off-topic but…. need a DDR4 laptop with non-soldered RAM - got a few spare sticks of laptop DDR4 laying around. All the HPs appear to have soldered RAM. Anyone can tell me where to look? Cheers lay-zeke-aunt
[Jack D Price] Remember kids, 5080 Laptop != 5080 Desktop
[Zenskas] This. The 5080 laptop 16GB GPU performs around the same as the desktop 5070 12GB. Chuck in the extra 4GB memory, it is equivalent to an imaginary desktop RTX 5070 16GB.
If the Omen doesn't power/cool the GPU enough to reach or maintain a high TDP at all times, then it could perform worse. Still, it's a pretty fast GPU for a laptop and shouldn't struggle hard in modern games.
[Propagandamachineru] According to reviews, the build quality is the worst among the big names, the pudding keyboard also isn’t my thing, guess hp had to cut corners to fit in a 5080
[sngr] Yep, I'd avoid buying anything of this value thru HP eBay as well, they will leave you on read for months if anything goes wrong with it
[sngr] The catch is that warranty doesn't count for anything if you use HP eBay as they will drag their feet for months and months
[GerrardLFC] Got this laptop in June for $2600 from office works on clearance.
Very good laptop and build quality is great. Got 3 years onsite warranty for $100 extra.
[jimbler] Wayyyyyy too much ram there. A data centre would make much better use of it! /altman
[moooz] It's an ok deal, but a few spec considerations (in order, for me, ymmv):
1. Small arrow keys. If you are left-handed, this is an absolute deal breaker. It's why I'll never buy it
2, No Thunderbolt 5
3. No bluetooth 6
4. Ram is a little slow at 5600 mt/s (but not bad, especially with 32gb)
5. Obviously a 1TB HDD is normal now, but a little small and only gen 4
6. OLED is not ideal for many use cases - burn in is still an issue. Would prefer mini LED.
7. No advanced optimus
Note: this is my personal preference, but you asked, so I'm laying it out. And again, this is in order of most important to least, for me.
There is no perfect laptop at the moment. But I prefer the Scar 16 and Alienware 16. They doubled in price though from when they were released.
